newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF eases on sale price concerns.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF eases on sale price concerns.

text.p: Shares in Thomson-CSF, the defence electronics arm of state-owned Thomson SA, eased on Monday on concerns the French government may decide to privatise Thomson-CSF through the sale of shares at a discount.

The government has not yet announced how it plans to privatise Thomson-CSF, but brokers said a share sale looks more likely since the state's decision last month to scrap an earlier plan to sell the entire Thomson group in one go.
Thomson-CSF shares were down 1.16 percent at 170 francs in a market that was modestly higher. The CAC index was up 0.3 percent.
One analyst said concerns were fuelled by a heavy supply of paper expected to land on the bourse in the first half of 1997, including the partial privatisation of France Telecom.

He also cited the price that had previously been offered to Thomson-CSF minority shareholders of 156 francs by Lagardere, which had been chosen by the government in October to buy the group. The sale plan was dropped after the privatisation commission objected to the terms, notably Lagardere's proposal to sell the Thomson Multimedia TV business to Daewoo Electronics of South Korea for one franc.
